extracted.intended_audience: registrants, corporate accounting and legal teams, auditors, and counsel preparing SEC filings involving real estate acquisitions (Form 8-K, S-11, S-4, proxy statements)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and filing abbreviated financial statements and related disclosures for acquisitions of real estate operations under Regulation S‑X Rule 3‑14, including significance tests, presentation rules, accommodations, audit considerations, and blind-pool specific rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance thresholds for real estate acquisitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the investment test condition specified in the definition of significant subsidiary in §210.1-02(w)(1)(i) as modified: (A) If the condition does not exceed 20 percent, financial statements are not required. (B) If the condition exceeds 20 percent, financial statements of the real estate operation for at least the most recent fiscal year and the most recent interim period must be filed. (C) If the aggregate impact of acquired or to be acquired real estate operations since the date of the most recent audited balance sheet exceeds 50 percent, the registrant must provide additional disclosures (see (b)(2)(i)(C)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the core significance framework: <=20% none; >20% historical year + most recent interim; >50% triggers pro forma and additional financial statements and disclosures. The 20% and 50% levels are computed per the modified investment test.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periods required when condition exceeds 20%
rubrics_metrics.description: If the condition exceeds 20 percent, financial statements are required of the real estate operation for at least the most recent fiscal year and the most recent interim period specified in §§ 210.3-01 and 210.3-02.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No comparative interim period of the prior year is required for the interim period — registrant must include most recent audited fiscal year and most recent unaudited interim period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregate 50% threshold disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: If the aggregate impact of acquired or to be acquired real estate operations since the date of the most recent audited balance sheet exceeds 50 percent, the registrant must provide: (1) Pro forma financial information pursuant to §§ 210.11-01 through 210.11-02 showing aggregate impact; and (2) Financial statements covering at least the most recent fiscal year and the most recent interim period for any acquired or to be acquired real estate operation for which financial statements are not yet required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there are also businesses acquired as described in §210.3-05(b)(2)(iv), the requirements in §210.3-05(b)(2)(iv) will apply instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include assumed debt in investment test when based on total assets
rubrics_metrics.description: When the investment test is based on total assets of the registrant and its subsidiaries consolidated, include any assumed debt secured by the real properties in the 'investments in' the tested real estate operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This modifies the numerator of the investment test to reflect assumed liabilities secured by the real estate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method of determination reference
rubrics_metrics.description: The determination of significance must be made using §210.11-01(b)(3) and (4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the referenced section's computation and rules when applying the investment and asset tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omission rules for certain registration and proxy statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration statements not subject to §230.419 and proxy statements need not include separate financial statements of the acquired or to be acquired real estate operation if neither the operation nor the aggregate impact exceeds the condition of significance (as modified) at the 50 percent level computed in accordance with paragraph (b)(2), and either (A) consummation has not yet occurred; or (B) the date of the final prospectus/prospectus supplement or mailing date of a proxy is no more than 74 days after consummation and the financial statements have not previously been filed by the registrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides limited situations where separate financials may be omitted for filings such as registration statements and proxy statements — be careful with the 74-day window and prior filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing deadline for omitted financial statements (Form 8-K)
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant (other than a foreign private issuer) that omits financial statements of a recently consummated acquisition pursuant to the omission rule must file those financial statements and any pro forma information required by §§210.11-01 through 210.11-03 under cover of Form 8-K no later than 75 days after consummation of the acquisition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you relied on the omission carve-out at initial registration, you must still file the omitted financials on Form 8-K within 75 days after consummation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omission once operating results reflected for nine months
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate financial statements of the acquired real estate operation need not be presented once the operating results of the acquired real estate operation have been reflected in the audited consolidated financial statements of the registrant for at least nine months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mirrors S-X Rule 3-05 step-acquisition/consolidation principles — after nine months of post-acquisition consolidation, separate audited statements are no longer required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible presentation: revenues and certain expenses only
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial statements prepared and audited in accordance with Regulation S-X may be only statements of revenues and expenses excluding expenses not comparable to the proposed future operations (such as mortgage interest, leasehold rental, depreciation, amortization, corporate overhead and income taxes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other basic financial statements (e.g., statement of cash flows) are not required under S-X Rule 3-14; registrants may exclude historically non-comparable items but must disclose the exclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notes must disclose omitted expenses and comparability
rubrics_metrics.description: Notes to the financial statements must include: (i) the type of omitted expenses and the reason(s) why they are excluded; (ii) a description of how the financial statements presented are not indicative of future operating results because of the omitted expenses; and (iii) information about the real estate operation's operating, investing and financing cash flows, to the extent available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be specific about what was omitted and why, and explain limitations of comparability. Provide cash flow information if meaningful and available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign real estate operation financial statement accommodations
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial statements of an acquired or to be acquired foreign business that is a real estate operation and meets Item 17 of Form 20-F may satisfy S-X Rule 3-14. Such financial statements may be reconciled to U.S. GAAP or IFRS-IASB if the registrant is a foreign private issuer that prepares under IFRS-IASB. Reconciliations must generally follow Item 17(c) of Form 20-F; accommodations inconsistent with IFRS-IASB may not be applied, and IFRS 1 may be applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the acquired operation would itself qualify as a foreign private issuer, its FS may be prepared under IFRS-IASB without reconciliation to U.S. GAAP. Follow Form 20-F Item 17 guidance and avoid inconsistent accommodations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental information: material factors considered
rubrics_metrics.description: For each real estate operation for which financial statements are required, material factors considered by the registrant in assessing the operation must be described with specificity, including sources of revenue (including competition in the rental market, comparative rents, occupancy rates) and expense (including utility rates, property tax rates, maintenance expenses, anticipated capital improvements). The disclosure must also indicate that the registrant is not aware of any other material factors that would cause the reported financial statements not to be indicative of future operating results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specific operational and market information; explicitly state there are no other material factors known that would undermine the indicative value of the presented historical statements. Instruction 1: For Form S-11, supplement Item 15 disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors that may render statements not indicative
rubrics_metrics.description: The SEC staff has noted factors that would cause the financial statements to not be indicative of future operating results include: a change in how the real estate will be used; an expected material modification to the real estate; or a material change in property tax assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any of these are present, disclose and consider whether historical statements remain indicative or whether additional disclosures or omitted statements are appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pro forma financial information requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Pro forma financial information is required in accordance with S-X Article 11 when triggered (e.g., aggregate impact exceeding 50% or other significance situations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare pro forma under §§210.11-01 through 210.11-03 to depict aggregate impacts in all material respects; include with filings as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rolling 12-month financial statements prohibited
rubrics_metrics.description: No — the audited financial statements of a significant real estate operation under S-X Rule 3-14 must reflect the fiscal year-end of the real estate operation. A registrant may not provide audited FS for a rolling 12-month period before the acquisition in lieu of the latest fiscal year-end, nor combine pre- and post-acquisition periods to produce full-year FS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not substitute rolling 12-months or combined periods for a proper fiscal-year audited statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age considerations (staleness)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are no special age considerations under S-X Rule 3-14; the required age of FS is the same as S-X Rule 3-05.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the staleness/age rules applicable to S-X Rule 3-05 when determining whether financials are stale and need updating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cash flow presentation not required but disclose meaningful cash flow info if available
rubrics_metrics.description: S-X Rule 3-14 does not require a statement of cash flows. However, the SEC believes there may be cash flow information that would be meaningful to investors that should be disclosed if available (e.g., historical cash flows for capital improvements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide cash flow information to the extent it is meaningful and available, particularly for items like capital improvements; do not treat absence of a cash flow statement as prohibition on disclosing meaningful cash flow data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accommodations for limited leasing history or redevelopment
rubrics_metrics.description: Accommodations: If rental history is fewer than nine months but more than three months, FS may be presented on an unaudited basis. If the registrant acquires a property with no prior leasing history (previously owner-occupied or newly constructed), FS are not required; if leasing history is fewer than three months, FS are not required. If the property will be demolished and replaced, the staff would not object to omission of FS if prior revenues and costs are not representative — registrant should explain the omission. In other cases the registrant may request relief from the SEC staff in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these specific accommodations carefully: unaudited presentation allowed between 3–9 months of history; no FS required for no or <3 months leasing history; explain omissions for demolition/rebuild and consider requesting CF-OCA relief where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: S-X Rule 3-14 financial statements satisfy Schedule 14A Item 14 in proxies
rubrics_metrics.description: S-X Rule 3-14 financial statements of acquired or probable-to-be acquired real estate operations may be provided in lieu of S-X Rule 3-05 financial statements in proxy statements and, in applying Item 14 of Schedule 14A, registrants must ensure MD&A discusses operating trends depicted by historical FS and applicable property information described under Items 14 and 15 of Form S-11.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using 3-14 FS in a proxy, expand MD&A and other proxy disclosures as required by Item 14 and Form S-11 Items 14/15 to cover operating trends and property info.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting required for increases in equity interest (step acquisitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: An increase in equity interest of an existing subsidiary requires analysis: if the registrant consolidates the subsidiary and its operating results have been reflected in audited consolidated FS for at least nine months, separate audited FS are not required for the additional investment, although pro forma info may be required. If the registrant currently does not consolidate its investment, audited FS are required at the time of subsequent significant acquisitions regardless of whether control is obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the nine-month consolidation rule and consider whether pro forma information would be material and thus required; see examples for consolidating vs equity interest scenarios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit considerations for abbreviated financial statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Auditors ordinarily will issue a report on one or more specified elements, accounts, or items of a financial statement under AU-C 805 or AS 3305 when items (e.g., mortgage interest, depreciation) are excluded. Registrants may request relief from the audit requirement for FS of real estate operations with rental history of less than one year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect element-specific audit reports for abbreviated statements; consider and document any request for audit relief for short rental-history properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blind pool offerings: adapted significance tests and undertakings
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants conducting blind pool offerings (Industry Guide 5 subject) apply adapted significance tests under S-X Rule 11-01(b)(4). The income test does not apply; the investment test and asset test are modified (e.g., include expected proceeds in denominator during distribution period). Undertakings include filing sticker supplements during distribution period, consolidating stickers into post-effective amendments at least quarterly, disclosing compensation/fees received by GP(s), and filing audited FS for properties acquired during the distribution period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Blind-pool registrants must follow special adapted tests and ongoing disclosure undertakings during and after the distribution period; follow Industry Guide 5 undertakings such as quarterly post-effective amendments and disclosure of fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of distribution period for blind pool offerings
rubrics_metrics.description: The distribution period is the period during which the registrant is conducting a continuous 1933 Act registered offering through a registration statement subject to Industry Guide 5 — i.e., the period during which the securities registered in the blind pool offering are being sold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether an acquisition occurs during or after the distribution period because significance tests and accommodations differ by timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investment test for blind-pool real estate offerings without AWMV
rubrics_metrics.description: For blind-pool real estate offerings where registrant lacks an AWMV (non-traded REITs), S-X Rule 11-01(b)(4) allows an adapted investment test: numerator = investments in and advances to the acquired business + any assumed debt secured by the real properties; denominator = registrant’s consolidated total assets as of acquisition date + proceeds (net of commissions) expected to be raised in the registered offering over the next 12 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The registrant calculates numerator consistent with other acquisitions; include expected offering proceeds in denominator to avoid classifying small early acquisitions as significant simply because registrant initially owns few assets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimating offering proceeds during distribution period
rubrics_metrics.description: In estimating offering proceeds, the SEC staff has stated registrant should consider the pace of fundraising as of the measurement date, the sponsor or dealer-manager's prior public fundraising experience, and offerings by similar entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reasonable, supportable estimates of expected proceeds (pace, sponsor history, peer offerings) when applying adapted blind-pool denominator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of acquired business assets from denominator
rubrics_metrics.description: When determining significance (in blind-pool or other contexts described), registrants should not include the acquired business’s assets in the denominator when S-X Rule 11-01 requires exclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For adapted blind-pool denominator rules and certain periods, exclude the assets of the acquired business from the denominator per the rule text to compute significance correctly.
